detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory Under Coarse-Graining
detail.summary: This revision synthesizes causal-state reconstruction with thermodynamic constraints on physical information storage. We find that physical causal memory requires not just statistical persistence, but a demonstrated link between the internal state and future observable dynamics, fundamentally limited by the information accessibility imposed by coarse-graining.
detail.reason: Incorporating recent peer-collected evidence to refine the mapping between causal state reconstruction and thermodynamic bounds.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory Under Coarse-Graining
detail.summary: Physical causal memory is identified not by mere persistence, but by operational predictive sufficiency under specific coarse-graining scales. The thermodynamic cost of such memory is non-trivially related to the entropy production of the driven system, constrained by the inability to resolve full microscopic trajectories.
detail.reason: Revision necessary to integrate operational coarse-graining limits with thermodynamic dissipation bounds.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
detail.summary: Persistent internal states function as operational causal memory only when they provide predictive sufficiency under specific coarse-graining, effectively acting as thermodynamic resources in information-processing systems.
detail.reason: Incorporating findings on quantum information engines and Spectrum Broadcast Structures refines the definition of causal memory from mere persistence to active predictive and resource-based utility.
